meta.title: (A)phantasia and Severely Deficient Autobiographical Memory: Scientific and Personal Perspectives
meta.domain: Cognitive neuroscience / first-person phenomenology — aphantasia and severely deficient autobiographical memory
meta.overview: Hybrid single-case first-person report and scientific review by an author who was one of the three original SDAM subjects of Palombo et al. (2015) and is also aphantasic. Combines lived-experience testimony with a review of imagery in the history of science and a heuristic model relating aphantasia and SDAM.
meta.abstract: A combined scientific-and-personal-perspective article on living with both aphantasia (absence of voluntary visual imagery) and Severely Deficient Autobiographical Memory (SDAM). The author, a subject in the original SDAM study, argues the two conditions are related but distinct, that SDAM reflects a specific deficit in episodic re-experiencing rather than recognition, and that lacking imagery need not be an educational or career disadvantage, illustrated with the history of imagery in physics and mathematics.

claims.statement: A significant minority of people lack voluntary mental imagery (aphantasia), and some otherwise-healthy people have severely deficient autobiographical memory (SDAM).
Aphantasia and SDAM are related but distinct: some aphantasic people have no autobiographical-memory deficit.
Aphantasia is associated (first-person) with a compensatory reliance on verbal and abstract over visual/concrete thought.
SDAM reflects a specific deficit in episodic re-experiencing, not in factual recognition, evidenced by the absence of a ~500 ms recognition-related ERP present in controls.
Aphantasia is not necessarily an educational or career disadvantage.
Dreaming and voluntary imagery likely depend on partly different neural circuits (brainstem-driven vs fronto-parietal executive).

contributions.typing_rationale: Detailed lived-experience account by an original SDAM study subject who is also aphantasic — a rare combined first-person report describing awareness limited to direct sensory input, 'unheard' words, and 'invisible imagery'.

Proposes a nested heuristic (voluntary aphantasia superset of total aphantasia superset of SDAM) as a hypothesis about how the conditions relate; explicitly provisional pending cases of SDAM with intact voluntary imagery.
Synthesizes historical evidence (Galton onward; Einstein, Dirac, Mandelbrot, Bourbaki) on the role of imagery and its absence in scientific and mathematical thought.

external_baselines.description: Bilateral hippocampal volume reduction typical of developmental amnesics (paper cites ~30-50%; midpoint 40%), Vargha-Khadem et al. 1997.

deltas.note: SDAM shows ~10% RIGHT-hippocampal reduction vs ~30-50% BILATERAL reduction in developmental amnesia. Negative delta (structural deviation far milder), consistent with SDAM's intact recognition and semantic memory — SDAM is a subtle variant, not a lesion amnesia.

sota.resolver_notes: Undermind semantic search (year_max=2018) surfaced Palombo et al. 2015 (the SDAM syndrome the author is a subject of) as the primary prior, Zeman 2015 (aphantasia) as the imagery-side prior, and Brons 2018 as a contemporaneous near-neighbor also linking SDAM/aphantasia/imagery in memory (likely uncited). As a hybrid first-person + review, finding-level overlap is moderate and the combined-condition testimony has no close precedent.
